reports.title: Cory pass gargoyle valley
reports.comment: quick: Hiked into Cory pass, back side into gargoyle valley had 30-60cm+ of wind affected, firm crust and faceted snow in the north side. Lots of snow covering that valley despite the summer conditions going up. Hikers could want avy gear...old Size 1.5 avy was noted about 50m wide 50cm deep and I couldn't see how far it ran, from about 2500m from a  steep north east aspect. Scrambling condition o…

reports.title: Early season Sunshine (Lookout)
reports.comment: quick: Hiked up the Sunshine access road up to Goats Eye, at which point you can transition to skins (although the road is icy and the snow on either side has a temp crust). Things improved around 2,250m around the base of TP Town - although we got a series of collapses (whumpfing) of the crust overlying the ground facets. Higher up in the alpine was a mixed bag - from powder to wind blown snow to…

reports.title: Snow observations, Sunshine Village
reports.comment: snowpack: Lots of whumpfing on the October 26 crust in treeline areas near Sunshine Village. Good surface snow quality in sheltered areas.

reports.title: auto: Quick Report
reports.comment: quick: Given the concerns for the October 26 crust over facets and whumping in most places traveling just at tree line. Decided that sticking to simple non avalanche terrain was best. Ski pen was 10cm. That said the skiing was fast and enjoyable on mellow terrain. Surface faceting and surface hoar developing at treeline and below.

reports.title: Sunshine - base of twin cairns
reports.comment: quick: Toured around the base of twin cairns in the SSV slack country to beat the crowds. Great snow on E and NE aspects with an HS of about 72cm. South-ish aspects were much thinner and less supportive (i.e. more rocks). Pit at 2325m on E aspect gave CTM12 SC down 45 on the Oct 26 crust with an HS of 72cm. Didn't do an ECT but felt like propagation wouldn't have been significant. No issues while …

reports.title: Wawa north slopes
reports.comment: quick: We skied a few laps on the northern slopes of wawa in the sunshine back country. Found shooting cracks and whumphing at all elevations. We came over a roll near the top of wawa to find two small avalanches. One was about 40m wide and had a path length of only about 15m. The other about 10m wide and 40m long. They were approximately 50m apart and had cracks running between them. Both running…

reports.title: Size 1.5 on NE aspect
reports.comment: quick: Size 1.5 NE aspect 50 wide 45 deep 80 long. On 26th crust. Skinning up.

reports.title: SSV Slackcountry - Twin Cairns, Grizzly trees, Quartz
reports.comment: quick: Toured in the SSV slackcountry - Twin Cairns Traverse - Grizzly Trees - Quartz ridge. Got some extensive whumpfing on our way to the N face of Twin Cairns on the flats which propagated at least 20m. Nothing to report on our way up to Twin Cairns via W face - slabby but stable. Ridge is in good shape - only had to take off the skis twice for a bit of a bootpack. Grizzly trees in great shape,…

reports.title: Sunshine Staff AST
reports.comment: snowpack: Continuous cracking and whumpfing as we hiked through low angle terrain. CTV (SP) down 20-30cm on SH repeated several times on 30 degree test rolls.

reports.title: Skier Remote Avalanche Wawa Bowl
reports.comment: avalanche: Close call for a group of two triggering the main feature of Wawa bowl from 5m on their approach. The crust and facets can be clearly seen as the bed surface.

The October 26 crust layer was the bed surface sitting at 20-30cm …

reports.title: Healy pass area remote trigger
reports.comment: quick: We skied to the Healy pass area and skied up to the unnamed peak to the immediate north of the meadow. Once we reached the ridge, our party heard two sets of whumpfs. The second whumpf set off a remote triggered slide. This slide was on the leeward side of the slope ~15 m away on a slope greater than 45 degrees. The slide was ~1-1.5, but we did not approach the edge of the ridge to fully as…

reports.title: Healy Pass
reports.comment:
quick: Given the recent storm snow, we chose to ride in the Healy Pass Glades. After getting some whumpfing on the uptrack, we dug a quick pit. Results are below:
20 degree slope, SE Aspect
100cm Snow Depth
2355m in Elevation
-10 degrees Celsius air temperature

reports.title: Monarch Ramparts Skier Triggered
reports.comment: incident: NE slope, at 2300m. Remote triggered from above by second skier. Stepped down to base. Size 1.0 to 1.5. No injuries.

reports.title: Healy Ck-Simpson Pass-2Cairins
reports.comment:
quick: Went for an exploration trip - not looking for turns. Healy Ck Trail was well trodden and hard packed. Broke trail toward Simpson Pass - we mostly stayed low in the valley in the morning shade, and along the side of the east ridge.
Wumph observations started in the trees as we went higher on the ridge above Simpson pass and again in the rock gardens behind 2 Cairins. Sun started to warm/me…

reports.title: Bourgeau Meadows
reports.comment: quick: We found good skiing on East aspects between 2000 and 2300m. We found wind hammered snow above 2300m on all aspects.  Extensive whumpfing on East aspects amongst the Larches. We rode mellow slopes and stayed away from anything convex. Creek approach was mostly filled in.

reports.title: SSV Healy Creek - Dinosaur head and Big V
reports.comment: quick: Toured Ffom SSV into Healy Creek. Some sloughing on the steep chute at Dinosaur Head - the lower part had ran a few days ago and snowpack was thin and facetted and barely covered the boulders. Went down secondary drain - much less HS than last year at same time but still really good. Skinned up Big V by working the terrain - the main path had slid all the way to mid way on the fan a few day…

reports.title: Wawa ridge NE
reports.comment: quick: Rode the Wizard chutes off Wawa. There was significant wind loading and I had my concerns about how much snow was there vs other years. It was very deep and we experienced very little sluffing. All in all it felt very stable so we ripped it hard and had one of the best runs ever.

reports.title: Massive Mountain
reports.comment:
quick: Went to the summit of Massive Mountain via the drainage to the north west from Redearth Creek Trailhead. Conditions are a mixed bag and the bag is big!

Lower forest has very low snow and is basically iso. Once getting to low treeline it starts to get better for travel. Mid/high treeline and low alpine feels more like a winter snowpack. A mix of facets/crust depending on aspect but most pla…

reports.title: Healy pass
reports.comment: quick: No significant obs to report. Started from Wawa and made our way to Simpson trees before going to Healy pass. Consistently probed an HS of 125cm on all aspects. Snowpack per report - no collapsing or cracking observed. Hit some features that were more faceted but only observed minor sloughing. Wind started picking up by mid afternoon and we experienced a few pulses of snow. From near Healy …

reports.title: Bourgeau Meadows
reports.comment: quick: Went up Bourgeau Meadows from Healy pass trail.  We found excellent snow on east and south aspects between 2450m and 1900m. Some wind protected steep SW aspects had a sun crust on it but it was very localized.  Had a few settlements along wind hammered ridges.

reports.title: Quartz - SSV
reports.comment: quick: Amazing conditions on Quartz hill - we bagged both summits and descended on E aspect of second summit. Snow quality was amazing - about 45cm of unconsolidated snow sitting on the remains of old wind slab that was decomposing. Winds were very light this am but picked up in pm and clouds rolled in. No significant obs - no power sluffing either on our way down 35+deg terrain. Some point releas…

reports.title: Quartz Ridge
reports.comment: quick: Let the corn harvest begin! Loaded Standish at 8:45 due to racing activity you can even catch an earlier lift! Skiing was fast due to a nice layer of fresh surface hoar and a supportive melt-freeze crust.  We did a couple laps on the east aspect of Quartz ridge and they were starting to soft up quite nicely at 10am.  Things were getting warm at 11:30 so we headed for some NW aspect skiing w…

reports.title: Howard Douglas / Eagle Basin (SSV)
reports.comment: quick: Good run up Howard Douglas today. Started with first gondola at 8am and snow was bullet proof all the way to the col (although col was softening up quite a bit by 11am so we turned around and skipped the summit).
